sources.name: Nepal BIPAD — verified disaster incidents
sources.notes: Government of Nepal public documented API. Factual metadata only: verified and approved records, positive actual impact, strict point containment, aggregate losses and provider ward IDs. Reported-date and descending modified-date lookbacks overlap one day, catch up at most seven days and reject incomplete/order-conflicting pages. Provider modified-date filters are ignored and are not used. New records before the published history window are held. Approved hazard profiles currently exclude rain, storms, lightning and animal incidents even when harm is reported; those require separate review. No blanket narrative/asset redistribution license asserted. No models, credentials or paid calls.

sources.name: CDC — disease outbreak notices
sources.notes: Source: CDC. Original source material is available free. Use does not imply endorsement by CDC, HHS or the United States Government. Complete public RSS and serialized complete notice details. Automatic intake uses five reviewed disease/country factual-statement profiles: Zika–Indonesia, hepatitis A–Costa Rica, yellow fever–Colombia, chikungunya–Costa Rica, and Rocky Mountain spotted fever–Mexico. New profiles, global/multi-country notices and changed unsupported statements require review. Geography comes only from the affirmative factual statement. CDC level is not incident severity. Earliest publication remains the date anchor, not outbreak onset. Revisions, disappearance and withdrawn/unsupported details retain evidence history; expiration is not resolution. Detail requests wait at least 20 seconds. No routine advice, images, models or paid services.

activationRequirements: Display CDC attribution/non-endorsement/free-original-source statement in source information; direct source links open a new tab.
Public collector must dispatch SECURITY_ADAPTERS and pass reviewed admin-places plus snapshot.history.from to collect_security_official.
Generic public-data reader source kinds rss/directory are used; no schema/category expansion.
CDC takes at least 20 seconds per explicit-country detail (currently five=100 seconds). Public-runner only; no Worker invocation or billing resource.
Keep actual raw response receipts locally or existing permitted collector evidence; never publish copied full pages or Nepal personal records.
knownLimitations: BIPAD uses validated descending modified-date pages because modified_on filters are silently ignored. More than ten pages or an outage beyond seven days requires bounded recovery; failures do not partially commit.
Separate loss-only edits are not guaranteed to change parent incident modifiedOn; such edits outside the report/modification overlap still need periodic retained-ID reconciliation.
BIPAD rain, storms, lightning and animal incidents are not yet reviewed for severe-harm inclusion; broad hazard coverage is not claimed.

CDC automatic intake is limited to five reviewed current factual-statement profiles. New profiles require review; ambiguous or changed content is held and previously admitted unsupported claims are expired/unverified.
CDC active notices retain accurate original publication dates and reported state. Older notices remain in history and may be absent from the 30-day overview pending a current-advisory design.
No total all-country or every-district category coverage claim.
